methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: A locally-branded AI readiness initiative in Roanoke signals grassroots capacity-building beyond traditional tech hubs, suggesting distributed fluency development if implementation reaches beyond evaluation to actual training and peer networks.

signals.title: AI is already common in Virginia Beach high schools. Leaders weigh guardrails - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: AI already embedded in Virginia Beach high schools with leaders now considering guardrails indicates platform-driven shallow adoption has already distributed broadly, with governance catching up to usage rather than capability-building leading deployment.

signals.title: VCU partners with the Better Business Bureau to bring AI support to Central Virginia businesses - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU partnering with BBB to deliver AI support concentrates expertise in Richmond's academic-business corridor, creating a hub-spoke model where Central Virginia businesses access centralized knowledge rather than building distributed internal capacity.

signals.title: Warner, Anthropic launch AI pilot to help Hampton Roads military families find local resources - The Legacy Newspaper
signals.signal_reading: Senator Warner deploying Anthropic's platform AI to serve military families represents shallow but high-impact distributed adoption—solving real problems through vendor tools rather than developing regional AI development capability.

signals.title: ODU, CHKD want to map hotspots of childhood asthma in Hampton Roads with AI - WHRO
signals.signal_reading: ODU and CHKD using AI for asthma mapping demonstrates deep technical application concentrated in research institutions, potentially widening the gap between university-led innovation and community-level AI fluency unless knowledge transfer occurs.
